title: Differential Expression Analysis Workflow with OmicsKit
text: vignette demonstrates complete RNA-seq differential expression analysis (DEA) workflow using OmicsKit, study design visualization, using real TCGA-LUAD data (16 tumor vs. 16 normal lung samples). workflow covers: Study design : statistical power estimation Quality control : unsupervised dimensionality reduction DEA results : annotation, normalization, export Visualization : volcano plots gene-level expression plots Multi-comparison : splitting genes exclusive expression cases

title: Differential Expression Analysis Workflow with OmicsKit
code: library(OmicsKit) library(ggplot2)

title: Differential Expression Analysis Workflow with OmicsKit
text: collecting data running analysis, good practice estimate minimum sample size needed reliably detect differentially expressed genes given effect size false discovery rate. power_analysis() computes statistical power across range sample sizes using analytical approximation accounts multiple testing:  Statistical power vs. sample size per group. red dashed line marks 80% power; blue dashed line marks minimum required sample size. TCGA-LUAD dataset used vignette 16 samples per group, well minimum required detecting log2FC ≥ 1 80% power.
code: result <- power_analysis(   effect_size  = 1,      # minimum log2 fold-change to detect   dispersion   = 0.1,    # biological coefficient of variation squared   n_genes      = 20000,  # total genes tested   prop_de      = 0.05,   # expected proportion of DE genes   alpha        = 0.05,   # desired FDR   power_target = 0.8,    # desired power (80%)   max_n        = 30,   plot         = TRUE )  # Minimum samples per group needed result$min_sample_size #> [1] 7  # Full power curve head(result$power_table) #>   SampleSize      Power #> 1          2 0.06234486 #> 2          3 0.20477735 #> 3          4 0.41078547 #> 4          5 0.61880322 #> 5          6 0.78217643 #> 6          7 0.88846759  # See plot result$plot

title: Differential Expression Analysis Workflow with OmicsKit
text: running DEA, essential verify samples cluster biological group detect potential batch effects outliers. OmicsKit provides three complementary dimensionality reduction methods accept VST-transformed count matrix. VST? Variance Stabilizing Transformation removes mean-variance dependence RNA-seq counts, placing genes comparable log2-like scale. prevents highly expressed genes dominating sample-level distances.
code: data(vst_counts) data(sampledata)  # nice_PCA, nice_UMAP, and nice_tSNE require a column named "id" sampledata_dim <- sampledata colnames(sampledata_dim)[colnames(sampledata_dim) == "patient_id"] <- "id"  dim(vst_counts) #> [1] 21330    32 table(sampledata$sample_type) #>  #> normal  tumor  #>     16     16

title: Differential Expression Analysis Workflow with OmicsKit
text: PCA fastest method always first step. first two principal components often capture main sources variation. PCA VST-transformed TCGA-LUAD counts. Tumor (red) normal (blue) samples separate cleanly along PC1.
code: nice_PCA(   object       = vst_counts,   annotations  = sampledata_dim,   variables    = c(fill = "sample_type"),   legend_names = c(fill = "Sample Type"),   colors       = c("steelblue", "firebrick"),   shapes       = c(21, 21),   title        = "TCGA-LUAD PCA: Tumor vs Normal" )

title: Differential Expression Analysis Workflow with OmicsKit
text: UMAP captures non-linear structure particularly useful larger datasets PCA show clear separation. UMAP VST-transformed TCGA-LUAD counts.
code: nice_UMAP(   object       = vst_counts,   annotations  = sampledata_dim,   variables    = c(fill = "sample_type"),   legend_names = c(fill = "Sample Type"),   colors       = c("steelblue", "firebrick"),   shapes       = c(21, 21),   title        = "TCGA-LUAD UMAP: Tumor vs Normal",   neighbors    = 5,   epochs       = 1000,   seed         = 174 )

title: Differential Expression Analysis Workflow with OmicsKit
text: tSNE useful visualizing tight local clusters. Note perplexity must less one-third number samples. tSNE VST-transformed TCGA-LUAD counts.
code: # With 32 samples, perplexity must be < 10 nice_tSNE(   object         = vst_counts,   annotations    = sampledata_dim,   perplexity     = 5,   max_iterations = 1000,   variables      = c(fill = "sample_type"),   legend_names   = c(fill = "Sample Type"),   colors         = c("steelblue", "firebrick"),   shapes         = c(21, 21),   title          = "TCGA-LUAD tSNE: Tumor vs Normal",   seed           = 174 )

Red: upregulated tumor; blue: downregulated; grey: significant.

title: Differential Expression Analysis Workflow with OmicsKit
text: detect_filter() identifies genes reliable expression levels applying thresholds baseMean mean normalized counts per group.
code: # detect_filter requires a column named "ensembl" res <- deseq2_results colnames(res)[colnames(res) == "gene_id"] <- "ensembl" rownames(res) <- res$ensembl  samples_normal <- sampledata$patient_id[sampledata$sample_type == "normal"] samples_tumor  <- sampledata$patient_id[sampledata$sample_type == "tumor"]  detected <- detect_filter(   norm.counts        = as.data.frame(norm_counts),   df.BvsA            = res,   samples.baseline   = samples_normal,   samples.condition1 = samples_tumor,   cutoffs            = c(50, 50, 0) )  length(detected$DetectGenes)

title: Differential Expression Analysis Workflow with OmicsKit
text: nice_VSB() shows distribution normalized expression single gene across sample groups. input normalized counts matrix. Note: alternative using DESeq2 object directly: still DESeqDataSet object session, can use nice_VSB_DESeq2() instead. extracts normalized counts internally via DESeq2::counts(dds, normalized = TRUE), need provide separate norm_counts matrix: Use nice_VSB() working pre-computed normalized counts matrix, nice_VSB_DESeq2() DESeq2 object still available environment. Violin-Scatter-Box plot significant DEG across tumor normal samples.
code: top_gene <- deseq2_results$gene_id[1]  # Get symbol #symbol <- deseq2_results$symbol[1]  nice_VSB(   object      = norm_counts,   annotations = sampledata,   variables   = c(fill = "sample_type"),   genename    = top_gene,   categories  = c("normal", "tumor"),   labels      = c("Normal", "Tumor"),   colors      = c("steelblue", "firebrick"),   shapes      = 21,   markersize  = 3 ) nice_VSB_DESeq2(   object     = dds,   variables  = c(fill = "sample_type"),   genename   = top_gene,   symbol     = "TP53",                 # optional: displayed in plot title   categories = c("normal", "tumor"),   labels     = c("Normal", "Tumor"),   colors     = c("steelblue", "firebrick"),   shapes     = 21,   markersize = 3 )

title: Differential Expression Analysis Workflow with OmicsKit
text: study includes three phenotypes (e.g., normal, primary tumor, metastasis), split_cases() classifies genes 10 mutually exclusive expression patterns based significance direction across three pairwise comparisons.
code: # Requires three DESeq2 result data frames: # df.BvsA : condition 1 vs baseline # df.CvsA : condition 2 vs baseline # df.BvsC : condition 1 vs condition 2  cases <- split_cases(   df.BvsA             = df_tumor_vs_normal,   df.CvsA             = df_meta_vs_normal,   df.BvsC             = df_tumor_vs_meta,   unique_id           = "ensembl",   significance_var    = "padj",   significance_cutoff = 0.05,   change_var          = "log2FoldChange",   change_cutoff       = 1 )  # Number of genes per case sapply(cases, nrow)  # Case 1: ladder genes : progressive up or down across all comparisons head(cases$Case1)

title: Differential Expression Analysis Workflow with OmicsKit
code: library(OmicsKit)  # 1. Study design power_analysis(effect_size = 1, dispersion = 0.1, n_genes = 20000)  # 2. QC: dimensionality reduction (use VST counts) data(vst_counts); data(sampledata) sampledata$id <- sampledata$patient_id  nice_PCA(vst_counts, sampledata, variables = c(fill = "sample_type"),          legend_names = c(fill = "Sample Type"),          colors = c("steelblue", "firebrick"), shapes = c(21, 21))  # 3. Annotate and export results annotations <- get_annotations(deseq2_results$gene_id) norm_counts_annot <- add_annotations(norm_counts, annotations) save_results(deseq2_results, name = "TumorVsNormal", l2fc = 1)  # 4. Visualize and filter non-detectable genes nice_Volcano(deseq2_results, x_var = "log2FoldChange",              y_var = "padj", label_var = "gene_id",              title = "Tumor vs Normal")  detected <- detect_filter(as.data.frame(norm_counts), deseq2_results,                           samples.baseline = samples_normal,                           samples.condition1 = samples_tumor)  nice_VSB(norm_counts, sampledata,          variables = c(fill = "sample_type"),          genename = detected$DetectGenes[1],          categories = c("normal", "tumor"),          labels = c("Normal", "Tumor"),          colors = c("steelblue", "firebrick"))  # 5. Multi-comparison (if 3 phenotypes) cases <- split_cases(df.BvsA, df.CvsA, df.BvsC)

title: TCGA-BRCA Clinical Modeling and Survival Workflow
text: vignette walks clinical modeling survival-analysis tools OmicsKit, applied clinical features TCGA-BRCA (Breast Invasive Carcinoma) cohort. Every model fit live clinical table code read code produced figure. workflow mirrors standard clinical-research pipeline: Exploratory survival profiling — time--event curves nice_KM(). Risk screening — univariable hazard ratios get_cox(). Risk summarization — forest plot every model term nice_forest(). Binary event prediction — logistic models get_glm(). Performance evaluation — model discrimination nice_ROC().

title: TCGA-BRCA Clinical Modeling and Survival Workflow
text: load package bundled clinical modeling table, build tidy analysis frame. TCGA clinical fields use empty strings missing values, convert NA front keep columns model. clinical endpoint used throughout Progression-Free Interval (PFI, event) follow-time (PFI.time, days):
code: library(OmicsKit)  data("brca_clinical_modeling_data")  model_vars <- c(   "PFI", "PFI.time",   "age_at_initial_pathologic_diagnosis",   "AJCC_stage_broad", "histological_type",   "menopause_status", "ER_group" )  brca_model <- brca_clinical_modeling_data[, intersect(model_vars, names(brca_clinical_modeling_data))]  # Treat empty strings as missing so factor levels are clean. brca_model[brca_model == ""] <- NA  # Collapse sparse categories so each level has enough events to model reliably. brca_model$histology <- ifelse(   brca_model$histological_type %in% c("Infiltrating Ductal Carcinoma",                                       "Infiltrating Lobular Carcinoma"),   brca_model$histological_type, "Other" ) brca_model$histology[is.na(brca_model$histological_type)] <- NA  brca_model$menopause <- ifelse(grepl("^Pre",  brca_model$menopause_status), "Pre",                         ifelse(grepl("^Post", brca_model$menopause_status), "Post", NA)) head(brca_model[, c("PFI.time", "PFI", "AJCC_stage_broad", "ER_group")]) #>   PFI.time PFI AJCC_stage_broad ER_group #> 1     1808   1             <NA>     <NA> #> 2     4005   0             <NA>     <NA> #> 3     1474   0             <NA>     <NA> #> 4     1448   0             <NA>     <NA> #> 5      348   0             <NA>     <NA> #> 6     1477   0             <NA>     <NA>

text: nice_KM() builds Kaplan-Meier curves annotates Log-rank p-value. stratify Progression-Free Interval broad AJCC tumor stage. Note argument names required function: grouping column goes gene, survival columns time_var / event_var. nice_KM() uses grouping column’s name (title_prefix) legend title, copy stage cleanly named column — Stage — keep legend free underscores, set title_prefix = "". Kaplan-Meier PFI curves TCGA-BRCA stratified broad AJCC tumor stage.
code: km_data <- brca_model[   !is.na(brca_model$AJCC_stage_broad) &     is.finite(brca_model$PFI.time) &     !is.na(brca_model$PFI),   ,   drop = FALSE ] km_data$Stage <- km_data$AJCC_stage_broad  plot_or_message(   nice_KM(     data         = km_data,     gene         = "Stage",     time_var     = "PFI.time",     event_var    = "PFI",     title_prefix = "",     colors       = c("#2A9D8F", "#457B9D", "#E9C46A", "#E63946"),     conf_int     = FALSE   ) )

text: nice_forest() turns tidy Cox table forest plot. default keeps every model term (p_display = 1), plot shows significant non-significant estimates — point forest plot see whole set effects confidence intervals side side, “winners”. plotting one cosmetic clean-: label columns carry database-style names underscores (AJCC_stage_broad, ER_positive, age_at_initial_pathologic_diagnosis). single gsub() step collapses run underscores one space across three columns nice_forest() uses build labels, nothing plot shows underscore: Univariable clinical Cox screen TCGA-BRCA PFI. Every model term shown; colour marks statistical significance.
code: # Replace single or repeated underscores with a single space for nicer labels. label_cols <- c("variable", "term_clean", "reference") cox_table[label_cols] <- lapply(cox_table[label_cols], function(x) gsub("_+", " ", x))  plot_or_message(   nice_forest(     data      = cox_table,     title     = "TCGA-BRCA Univariable Clinical Cox Screen (PFI)",     p_display = 1,     sort_by   = "estimate"   ) )

title: TCGA-BRCA Clinical Modeling and Survival Workflow
text: judge well baseline model separates progressors non-progressors, evaluate held-test split compare full clinical model age-baseline. nice_ROC() takes named list fitted glm objects plus evaluation data binary outcome. get_glm() stores fitted model attr(result, "model"), pass straight . ROC comparison progression classifier: full clinical model vs. age .
code: glm_frame <- brca_model[   !is.na(brca_model$PFI),   c("PFI", "AJCC_stage_broad", "age_at_initial_pathologic_diagnosis",     "ER_group", "histology", "menopause") ] glm_frame <- glm_frame[stats::complete.cases(glm_frame), , drop = FALSE]  set.seed(2025) train_idx <- sample(nrow(glm_frame), size = floor(0.6 * nrow(glm_frame))) train <- glm_frame[train_idx, , drop = FALSE] test  <- glm_frame[-train_idx, , drop = FALSE]  fit_full <- attr(   get_glm(     data       = train,     outcome    = "PFI",     predictors = c("AJCC_stage_broad", "age_at_initial_pathologic_diagnosis",                    "ER_group", "histology", "menopause")   ),   "model" )  fit_age <- attr(   get_glm(     data       = train,     outcome    = "PFI",     predictors = "age_at_initial_pathologic_diagnosis"   ),   "model" )  plot_or_message(   nice_ROC(     models     = list("Clinical model" = fit_full, "Age only" = fit_age),     data       = test,     outcome    = "PFI",     plot_title = "Progression Classifier — ROC"   ) )

title: TCGA-BRCA Omics-Layer Visualization
text: nice_GenomeTrack() function allows plot specific molecular features statistical metrics, log2 fold changes mutation frequencies, across individual chromosomes specific genomic regions. provides clear one-dimensional overview molecular changes spatially distributed across genome.
code: plot_or_message(   nice_GenomeTrack(     tracks = brca_omics_layer_tracks$genome_tracks   ) )

title: TCGA-BRCA Omics-Layer Visualization
text: global, multi-layered perspective entire genome, circular layout, commonly known Circos plot, widely used bioinformatics. nice_circos() function integrates multiple tracks, copy number variation, expression levels, clinical groups, single unified plot. Since rendering interactive highly detailed Circos plots package compilation can resource-intensive, code block set eval = FALSE. pre-rendered high-resolution static image can saved package figures directory rapid documentation rendering. title: TCGA-BRCA Pathway Analysis and Clustering Workflow
text: vignette demonstrates downstream workflow Pathway Analysis (e.g., GSEA) using OmicsKit, applied TCGA-BRCA dataset. workflow covers: Exploring enriched pathways using single multi-comparison visualizations (splot_PA, multiplot_PA). Extracting annotating genes pathway results (getgenesPA, addgenesPA). Visualizing gene-level expression inside selected pathways via heatmaps (heatmap_PA). Reducing redundancy computing pathway similarity clustering pathway terms (geneset_similarity, do_clust). Detecting network communities identifying biological super-terms (get_network_communities, network_clust_gg). Several computationally intensive visualizations shown pre-rendered static figures keep vignette compilation fast reproducible.

title: TCGA-BRCA Pathway Analysis and Clustering Workflow
text: First, load package pre-computed TCGA-BRCA objects provided data/ folder. Let’s take quick look merged pathway analysis results:
code: library(OmicsKit)  # Load pathway analysis results, gene set lists, and ranked genes data("brca_pa_merged") data("brca_geneset_list") data("brca_ranked_genes")  # Load pre-computed clustering and similarity objects data("brca_pa_similarity") data("brca_pa_clustering") table(brca_pa_merged$COMPARISON, brca_pa_merged$COLLECTION) #>                            #>                            GO_BP Hallmark #>   ERpositive_vs_ERnegative  3898       50 #>   Tumor_vs_Normal           3902       50

code:
pa_multi_subset <- subset(   brca_pa_merged,   COMPARISON %in% c("Tumor_vs_Normal", "ERpositive_vs_ERnegative") &     NAME %in% c(       "HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY",       "HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_LATE"     ) )  # Clean labels for display pa_multi_subset$PATHWAY_LABEL <- pa_multi_subset$NAME pa_multi_subset$PATHWAY_LABEL[   pa_multi_subset$NAME == "HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY" ] <- "Estrogen response
early" pa_multi_subset$PATHWAY_LABEL[   pa_multi_subset$NAME == "HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_LATE" ] <- "Estrogen response
late"  comparison_labels <- c(   "Tumor_vs_Normal" = "Tumor vs
Normal",   "ERpositive_vs_ERnegative" = "ER+ vs
ER-" )  multiplot_PA(   data             = pa_multi_subset,   comparison_col   = "COMPARISON",   facet_col        = "PATHWAY_LABEL",   axis_y           = "NES",   fdr_col          = "FDR",   comparison_order = c("Tumor_vs_Normal", "ERpositive_vs_ERnegative"),   custom_labels    = comparison_labels,   ncol_wrap        = 2,   free_y           = FALSE,   fill_limits      = c(0, 5),   theme_params     = list(     axis_title_size     = 13,     axis_text_size_x    = 10,     axis_text_size_y    = 10,     strip_text_size     = 11,     hline_size          = 0.6,     tick_size           = 0.4,     tick_length         = 0.12,     panel_spacing_multi = 0.8   ) )

title: TCGA-BRCA Pathway Analysis and Clustering Workflow
text: assign biological meaning pathway clusters, OmicsKit can detect communities within pathway similarity network extract representative biological super-terms. original similarity object contains multiple comparisons. vignette, network figures generated ERpositive_vs_ERnegative subset . keeps examples focused one biological contrast avoids mixing nodes multiple comparisons.
code: # Example code used during figure generation comparison <- "ERpositive_vs_ERnegative"  brca_pa_similarity_er <- brca_pa_similarity keep <- grepl(paste0("^", comparison, "::"), rownames(brca_pa_similarity$jaccard_sim))  brca_pa_similarity_er$jaccard_sim <- brca_pa_similarity$jaccard_sim[   keep,   keep,   drop = FALSE ]  # Remove the comparison prefix from node names for cleaner labels node_names <- sub(   paste0("^", comparison, "::"),   "",   rownames(brca_pa_similarity_er$jaccard_sim) )  rownames(brca_pa_similarity_er$jaccard_sim) <- make.unique(node_names) colnames(brca_pa_similarity_er$jaccard_sim) <- make.unique(node_names) brca_pa_similarity_er$dist_mat <- as.dist(1 - brca_pa_similarity_er$jaccard_sim)  brca_pa_clustering_er <- do_clust(brca_pa_similarity_er)  net_results_er <- get_network_communities(   x             = brca_pa_similarity_er,   threshold     = 0.3,   method        = "louvain",   superterms    = TRUE,   n_terms       = 3,   remove_prefix = TRUE,   seed          = 174 )  head(net_results_er$superterms$summary)  network_clust_gg(   x                 = brca_pa_similarity_er,   clust_result      = brca_pa_clustering_er,   jaccard_threshold = 0.3,   min_degree        = 1,   superterms        = TRUE,   superterm_data    = net_results_er$superterms,   type              = "superterms",   seed              = 174 )

title: Pathway Analysis Clustering with OmicsKit
text: geneset_similarity() filters gene sets FDR threshold computes pairwise Jaccard similarity coefficients: J(,B)=|∩B||∪B|J(, B) = \frac{|\cap B|}{|\cup B|} value 1 means two gene sets share identical gene membership; 0 means overlap . $dist_mat slot (1 − Jaccard similarity) can reused independently — example input nice_UMAP() distance-based method.
code: jac <- geneset_similarity(   geneset_list  = geneset_list,   results       = camera_results,   fdr_th        = 0.05 )  # The JaccardResult object contains three slots names(jac) #> [1] "jaccard_sim"  "dist_mat"     "geneset_list"  # Dimensions of the similarity matrix dim(jac$jaccard_sim) #> [1] 24 24 # Preview the top-left corner of the similarity matrix jac$jaccard_sim[1:5, 1:5] #>                        KEGG_APOPTOSIS HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS GO_INTRINSIC_APOPTOSIS #> KEGG_APOPTOSIS             1.00000000         0.43478261             0.39130435 #> HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS         0.43478261         1.00000000             0.52631579 #> GO_INTRINSIC_APOPTOSIS     0.39130435         0.52631579             1.00000000 #> GO_EXTRINSIC_APOPTOSIS     0.31818182         0.08333333             0.04166667 #> HALLMARK_P53_PATHWAY       0.06666667         0.16000000             0.12000000 #>                        GO_EXTRINSIC_APOPTOSIS HALLMARK_P53_PATHWAY #> KEGG_APOPTOSIS                     0.31818182           0.06666667 #> HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS                 0.08333333           0.16000000 #> GO_INTRINSIC_APOPTOSIS             0.04166667           0.12000000 #> GO_EXTRINSIC_APOPTOSIS             1.00000000           0.00000000 #> HALLMARK_P53_PATHWAY               0.00000000           1.00000000

title: Pathway Analysis Clustering with OmicsKit
text: Hierarchical clustering groups gene sets overall similarity, network community detection captures different structure: densely connected sub-networks within Jaccard graph. get_network_communities() three things single call: Builds binary adjacency matrix (edges Jaccard > threshold) Runs Louvain algorithm detect communities Calls get_superterm() internally generate TF-IDF labels community $superterms$mapping tibble links every gene set community super-term label:
code: net <- get_network_communities(   x             = jac,   threshold     = 0.3,   method        = "louvain",   superterms    = TRUE,   n_terms       = 3,   remove_prefix = TRUE,   seed          = 1905 )  # How many communities were detected? title: Pathway Analysis Workflow with OmicsKit
text: vignette demonstrates complete gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) downstream workflow using OmicsKit, loading gene sets publication-quality visualization. workflow covers: Loading gene sets : reading GMT files list_gmts() Merging results : combining multi-collection GSEA TSV files merge_PA() Gene extraction : retrieving leading edge top-ranked genes getgenesPA() annotating results addgenesPA() Heatmaps : visualizing gene expression per pathway heatmap_PA() (file-path alternative: heatmap_path_PA()) Single-comparison plot : splot_PA() : publication-quality multi-panel barplot one comparison Multi-comparison plot : multiplot_PA() : faceted barplots comparing enrichment across conditions

title: Pathway Analysis Workflow with OmicsKit
code: library(OmicsKit) library(ggplot2)

title: Pathway Analysis Workflow with OmicsKit
text: Gene sets used enrichment analysis stored .gmt files, standard format used MSigDB. list_gmts() reads .gmt files directory returns single named list, ready downstream use. vignette, use built-example geneset_list, contains 40 curated gene sets across four biological themes (apoptosis, cell cycle, immune response, metabolism), built-gsea_results dataset, mimics output merge_PA() three comparisons across HALLMARK, KEGG, GO collections.
code: geneset_list <- list_gmts("path/to/your/gmt_folder/")  # Number of gene sets loaded length(geneset_list) # Names of the first five gene sets names(geneset_list)[1:5] # Genes in one specific set geneset_list[["HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE"]] data(geneset_list) data(gsea_results) data(deseq2_results) data(vst_counts) data(sampledata) # Ranked gene list: DESeq2 Wald stat from most positive to most negative ranked_genes <- deseq2_results$gene_id[   order(deseq2_results$stat, decreasing = TRUE) ] # Overview of the enrichment results dim(gsea_results) #> [1] 120  15 unique(gsea_results$COMPARISON) #> [1] "TumorVsNormal"      "MetastasisVsNormal" "MetastasisVsTumor" unique(gsea_results$COLLECTION) #> [1] "HALLMARK" "KEGG"     "GO"

title: Pathway Analysis Workflow with OmicsKit
text: real analysis, GSEA produces one results file per MSigDB collection (e.g., H.tsv HALLMARK, C2.tsv KEGG). merge_PA() reads .tsv files directory, standardizes column names, parses leading edge string numeric components (tags, list, signal), computes -log10(FDR), returns single combined data frame. Note: .tsv file must contain Comparison column identifying comparison name (e.g., "TumorVsNormal"). merge_PA() renames COMPARISON. files come single run without column, add manually: built-gsea_results already structure:
code: gsea_data <- merge_PA(   input_directory = "path/to/gsea_results/",   fdr_replace     = 0.001   # replace FDR = 0 (below permutation resolution) ) # Inspect result head(gsea_data[, c("NAME", "NES", "FDR", "COLLECTION", "COMPARISON", "tags")]) your_data$Comparison <- "TumorVsNormal" # Key columns produced by merge_PA() head(gsea_results[, c("NES", "FDR", "Log10FDR",                       "COLLECTION", "COMPARISON", "tags", "SIZE")], n = 2) #>                             NES        FDR  Log10FDR COLLECTION    COMPARISON #> HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS   1.69000339 0.02526288 1.5975172   HALLMARK TumorVsNormal #> HALLMARK_P53_PATHWAY 0.08454987 0.82178574 0.0852414   HALLMARK TumorVsNormal #>                            tags SIZE #> HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS   0.60000000   15 #> HALLMARK_P53_PATHWAY 0.06963633   14

title: Pathway Analysis Workflow with OmicsKit
text: obtaining pathway results, getgenesPA() retrieves gene members relevant enrichment signal. Three extraction modes available: - "le" (GSEA ): leading edge genes : subset drives enrichment score. - "top": top-ranked n % genes rank metric : applicable enrichment method (GSEA, CAMERA, PADOG, etc.). - "": members gene set, ordered rank. addgenesPA() appends gene lists comma-separated columns (le_genes, top_genes, all_genes) pathway results table. Tip: CAMERA enrichment methods produce leading edge information, use genes = c("", "top") set pa_data$top desired fraction (e.g., 0.25 top 25 % rank). request genes = "le" without tags column.
code: # Filter to one comparison pa_single <- gsea_results[gsea_results$COMPARISON == "TumorVsNormal", ] # Optional: define the top fraction for mode "top" pa_single$top <- 0.30   # top 30% of gene set members by rank # Extract genes using all three modes gene_lists <- getgenesPA(   pa_data      = pa_single,   geneset_list = geneset_list,   ranked_genes = ranked_genes,   genes        = c("all", "le", "top") ) # Inspect results for one pathway   ## leading edge   gene_lists$le[["HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE"]]    ## top 30% by rank   gene_lists$top[["HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE"]]     ## all members   gene_lists$all[["HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE"]]   # Append gene columns to the pathway table pa_annot <- addgenesPA(pa_single, gene_lists) # Number of gene sets annotated nrow(pa_annot)  head(pa_annot[, c("NAME", "all_genes", "le_genes", "top_genes")])

title: Pathway Analysis Workflow with OmicsKit
text: heatmap_PA() generates one heatmap per gene set based pa_data_annot. Genes ordered within heatmap position ranked_genes. Output files organized subdirectories format (PDF / JPG) gene selection mode (all_genes, le_genes, top_genes). heatmap shows top-ranked genes HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE across tumor normal TCGA-LUAD samples: Expression heatmap top-ranked genes HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE across TCGA-LUAD tumor normal samples. Genes ordered DESeq2 Wald statistic.
code: heatmap_PA(   expression_data = vst_counts,   metadata        = sampledata,   pa_data_annot   = pa_annot,   ranked_genes    = ranked_genes,   plot_genes      = c("all_genes", "le_genes", "top_genes"),   sample_col      = "patient_id",   group_col       = "sample_type",   out_dir         = "heatmaps_PA",   pdf             = TRUE,   jpg             = TRUE ) # Creates, for example: #   heatmaps_PA/jpg/top_genes/HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE_heatmap.jpg #   heatmaps_PA/pdf/le_genes/HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE_heatmap.pdf #   ... (one file per gene set per format per mode)

title: Pathway Analysis Workflow with OmicsKit
text: heatmap_path_PA() convenience wrapper reads inputs disk (expression TSV, metadata XLSX, GMT file, ranked-genes TSV, GSEA TSV) calls heatmap engine internally. useful running analysis immediately GSEA without loading data R. function use? Prefer heatmap_PA() data already R (e.g., calling merge_PA(), getgenesPA(), addgenesPA()). Use heatmap_path_PA() want quick one-call solution reads directly files disk. functions produce identical heatmaps.
code: heatmap_path_PA(   main_dir          = "path/to/analysis/",   expression_file   = "vst_expression.tsv",   metadata_file     = "metadata.xlsx",   gmt_file          = "h.all.v2023.symbols.gmt",   ranked_genes_file = "ranked_genes.tsv",   gsea_file         = "H.tsv",   output_dir        = "leading_edge_heatmaps",   sample_col        = "patient_id",   group_col         = "sample_type",   save_dataframe    = TRUE   # also saves intermediate gene table as .tsv ) # Produces the same output as heatmap_PA() for a single GSEA file

title: Pathway Analysis Workflow with OmicsKit
text: splot_PA() generates publication-quality multi-panel enrichment plot one comparison. Gene sets appear y-axis (grouped MSigDB collection), NES x-axis, −log10(FDR) fill color. Six panels assembled side--side using patchwork. Single-comparison pathway enrichment plot (TumorVsNormal). Gene sets sorted NES; fill color encodes -log10(FDR), capped 2. Collections annotated right. Tip: Use fill_limits = c(0, 2) prevent handful extremely significant gene sets washing color contrast rest. pathway FDR ≤ 0.01 shown maximum color (red).
code: single <- gsea_results[gsea_results$COMPARISON == "TumorVsNormal", ] splot_PA(   data           = single,   geneset_col    = "NAME",   collection_col = "COLLECTION",   nes_col        = "NES",   fdr_col        = "FDR",   order          = "desc",   fill_limits    = c(0, 2),         # cap at -log10(FDR) = 5   fill_palette   = c("white", "red") )

title: Pathway Analysis Workflow with OmicsKit
text: multiplot_PA() generates faceted barplot showing NES across multiple comparisons selected set gene sets. facet represents one gene set; bars represent NES per comparison, colored −log10(FDR). layout makes straightforward assess enrichment changes across conditions. Multi-comparison pathway enrichment plot. facet shows NES one HALLMARK gene set across three pairwise comparisons. Fill color encodes -log10(FDR), capped 5. Tip: Use comparison_order control left--right arrangement comparisons x-axis facet, custom_labels replace long comparison names shorter axis labels.
code: # Subset to pathways of interest across all comparisons pathways_of_interest <- c(   "HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE",   "HALLMARK_INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE",   "HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT",   "HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS",   "HALLMARK_GLYCOLYSIS",   "HALLMARK_OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION" ) multi_data <- gsea_results[gsea_results$NAME %in% pathways_of_interest, ] multiplot_PA(   data             = multi_data,   comparison_col   = "COMPARISON",   facet_col        = "NAME",   axis_y           = "NES",   fdr_col          = "FDR",   comparison_order = c("TumorVsNormal",                        "MetastasisVsNormal",                        "MetastasisVsTumor"),   custom_labels    = c(     TumorVsNormal       = "Tumor",     MetastasisVsNormal  = "Meta",     MetastasisVsTumor   = "Meta/Tumor"   ),   ncol_wrap        = 3,   free_y           = TRUE,   fill_limits      = c(0, 5),   fill_palette     = c("white", "red") )

title: Pathway Analysis Workflow with OmicsKit
code: library(OmicsKit)  #  1. Load gene sets  gsl <- list_gmts("path/to/gmt_folder/")  # 2. Merge GSEA output TSV files  gsea_data <- merge_PA(   input_directory = "path/to/gsea_results/",   fdr_replace     = 0.001 ) # 3. Build ranked gene list (from DESeq2 stat or log2FC)  ranked <- deseq2_results$gene_id[   order(deseq2_results$stat, decreasing = TRUE) ] # 4. Extract leading edge and top-ranked genes  pa_single     <- gsea_data[gsea_data$COMPARISON == "TumorVsNormal", ] pa_single$top <- 0.30 gene_lists <- getgenesPA(pa_single, gsl, ranked, genes = c("all", "le", "top")) pa_annot   <- addgenesPA(pa_single, gene_lists) # 5. Heatmaps  heatmap_PA(   expression_data = vst_counts,   metadata        = sampledata,   pa_data_annot   = pa_annot,   ranked_genes    = ranked,   plot_genes      = c("all_genes", "le_genes", "top_genes"),   sample_col      = "patient_id",   group_col       = "sample_type",   out_dir         = "heatmaps_PA" ) # Alternative: file-path version (reads directly from disk) heatmap_path_PA(   main_dir          = "path/to/analysis/",   expression_file   = "vst_expression.tsv",   metadata_file     = "metadata.xlsx",   gmt_file          = "h.all.v2023.symbols.gmt",   ranked_genes_file = "ranked_genes.tsv",   gsea_file         = "H.tsv",   output_dir        = "leading_edge_heatmaps" ) # 6. Single-comparison enrichment plot splot_PA(   data           = pa_single,   geneset_col    = "NAME",   collection_col = "COLLECTION",   nes_col        = "NES",   fdr_col        = "FDR",   fill_limits    = c(0, 5) ) # 7. Multi-comparison enrichment plot pathways_oi <- c(   "HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE",   "HALLMARK_INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE",   "HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT" ) multiplot_PA(   data             = gsea_data[gsea_data$NAME %in% pathways_oi, ],   comparison_col   = "COMPARISON",   facet_col        = "NAME",   fdr_col          = "FDR",   comparison_order = c("TumorVsNormal", "MetastasisVsNormal", "MetastasisVsTumor"),   ncol_wrap        = 3 )

title: TCGA-BRCA RNA & RPPA: Differential Expression, Concordance and Visualization
text: Power analysis useful first check running large differential-expression analysis. TCGA-BRCA includes roughly 1100 tumor samples 113 adjacent normal samples, analysis still tests 20,000 genes simultaneously. Bulk RNA-seq studies often show biological dispersion near 0.1, even well-powered cohort needs multiple-testing correction mind. estimate minimum per-group sample size needed detect log2 fold-change 1 80% power.  Power analysis bulk RNA-seq differential-expression workflow TCGA-BRCA-like assumptions. TCGA-BRCA N >> minimum required, giving high power detect even modest fold-changes.
code: pa_result <- power_analysis(   effect_size  = 1,       # log2FC = 1 detectable minimum   dispersion   = 0.1,     # typical bulk RNA-seq biological variance   n_genes      = 20000,   prop_de      = 0.05,    # ~5% DE expected   alpha        = 0.05,   power_target = 0.8,   max_n        = 30,   plot         = TRUE )  cat("Minimum samples per group needed:", pa_result$min_sample_size, "\n") #> Minimum samples per group needed: 7 pa_result$plot ggplot2::ggsave("vignettes/figures/power_analysis.png",        pa_result$plot, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 150)  grDevices::pdf("vignettes/figures/power_analysis.pdf",                width = 8, height = 5) print(pa_result$plot) grDevices::dev.off()

title: TCGA-BRCA RNA & RPPA: Differential Expression, Concordance and Visualization
text: Integrating RNA-seq RPPA data comparison allows us assess transcription--protein concordance. Genes concordant layers provide stronger evidence true biological change. OmicsKit provides three complementary functions: concordanceDE() classifies genes concordant, discordant, only_x, only_y, not_significant categories computes concordance score. crossLayerCorr() computes sample-level Spearman correlations two omics layers using variable shared features. nice_ConcordanceScatter() visualizes logFC-logFC relationship layers.

title: TCGA-BRCA RNA & RPPA: Differential Expression, Concordance and Visualization

title: Add gene columns to pathway analysis results — addgenesPA
code: addgenesPA(pa_data, gene_lists)

title: Add gene columns to pathway analysis results — addgenesPA
text: pa_data data frame pathway analysis results containing NAME column. Typically output merge_PA(). gene_lists Output getgenesPA(). Can : list $, $le, /$top slots: multiple modes requested (e.g., getgenesPA(..., genes = c("", "le", "top"))). Adds corresponding columns. flat named list attribute genes_type: single mode requested. Adds corresponding column (all_genes, le_genes, top_genes).

title: Add gene columns to pathway analysis results — addgenesPA
text: input pa_data data frame one additional columns: all_genes: comma-separated string gene set members ordered rank. le_genes: comma-separated string leading edge genes (GSEA ), ordered rank. top_genes: comma-separated string top-ranked genes based user-defined top fraction. Gene sets found gene_lists receive NA.

title: Add gene columns to pathway analysis results — addgenesPA
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ data(gsea_results) data(brca_geneset_list) data(brca_rna_dea_tumor_vs_normal)  ranked    <- brca_rna_dea_tumor_vs_normal$gene_id[order(brca_rna_dea_tumor_vs_normal$stat,                                           decreasing = TRUE)] pa_single <- gsea_results[gsea_results$COMPARISON == "TumorVsNormal", ] pa_single$top <- 0.30  # Add all three columns gene_lists <- getgenesPA(pa_single, brca_geneset_list, ranked,                          genes = c("all", "le", "top")) pa_annot   <- addgenesPA(pa_single, gene_lists) head(pa_annot[, c("NAME", "all_genes", "le_genes", "top_genes")])  # Add only leading edge genes le_only  <- getgenesPA(pa_single, brca_geneset_list, ranked, genes = "le") pa_annot <- addgenesPA(pa_single, le_only) head(pa_annot[, c("NAME", "le_genes")])  # CAMERA: add only top and all (no leading edge) data(brca_pa_results) camera_pa      <- brca_pa_results colnames(camera_pa)[colnames(camera_pa) == "GeneSet"] <- "NAME" camera_pa$SIZE <- sapply(camera_pa$NAME,                          function(x) length(brca_geneset_list[[x]])) camera_pa$top  <- 0.25 gene_lists_cam <- getgenesPA(camera_pa, brca_geneset_list, ranked,                              genes = c("all", "top")) pa_annot_cam   <- addgenesPA(camera_pa, gene_lists_cam) head(pa_annot_cam[, c("NAME", "all_genes", "top_genes")]) } # }

what: Classify differential results by cross-layer concordance. — concordanceDE
title: Classify differential results by cross-layer concordance. — concordanceDE
text: Compares two differential-analysis tables paired omics layers, RNA-seq total-protein RPPA, merging shared genes classifying gene according statistical significance log-fold-change direction.

title: Classify differential results by cross-layer concordance. — concordanceDE
code: concordanceDE(   de_x,   de_y,   gene_col = "gene",   logfc_col = "logFC",   padj_col = "padj",   padj_threshold = 0.05,   logfc_threshold = 1 )

title: Classify differential results by cross-layer concordance. — concordanceDE
text: de_x Data frame layer X. Must contain columns defined gene_col, logfc_col, padj_col. de_y Data frame layer Y. Must contain columns defined gene_col, logfc_col, padj_col. gene_col Column name containing gene identifiers. Default: "gene". logfc_col Column name containing log-fold changes. Default: "logFC". padj_col Column name containing adjusted p-values/FDR values. Default: "padj". padj_threshold Numeric threshold adjusted p-values. Use single value layers length-two vector layer X layer Y, respectively. Default: 0.05. logfc_threshold Numeric absolute log-fold-change threshold. Use single value layers length-two vector layer X layer Y, respectively. Default: 1.

title: Classify differential results by cross-layer concordance. — concordanceDE
text: list : table: merged data frame one category column. concordance_score: fraction genes significant layers matching log-fold-change direction. summary: table counts per concordance category. n_shared_genes: number genes shared layers. n_both_significant: number genes significant layers.

title: Classify differential results by cross-layer concordance. — concordanceDE
text: Genes assigned one five categories: concordant, discordant, only_x, only_y, not_significant. concordance score also computed fraction genes significant layers effect direction.

title: Classify differential results by cross-layer concordance. — concordanceDE
code: de_rna <- data.frame(   gene = c("ESR1", "PGR", "EGFR", "MKI67", "GATA3"),   logFC = c(3.2, 2.1, -1.6, -1.4, 1.8),   padj = c(1e-6, 0.002, 0.01, 0.03, 0.04) )  de_protein <- data.frame(   gene = c("ESR1", "PGR", "EGFR", "MKI67", "GATA3"),   logFC = c(0.7, 0.4, -0.5, 0.3, 0.05),   padj = c(1e-4, 0.01, 0.02, 0.04, 0.40) )  res <- concordanceDE(   de_x = de_rna,   de_y = de_protein,   logfc_threshold = c(1, 0.2) ) res$summary #>  #>      concordant      discordant          only_x          only_y not_significant  #>               3               1               1               0               0  res$concordance_score #> [1] 0.75

title: Find detectable genes across comparisons. — detect_filter
text: norm.counts Data frame normalized counts Ensembl IDs rows Sample IDs columns. df.BvsA Data frame comparing first condition baseline. df.CvsA Data frame comparing second condition baseline (optional). df.DvsA Data frame comparing third condition baseline (optional). cutoffs Vector containing threshold values baseMean, mean normalized counts Log2 Fold Change; respectively. Default: c(50, 50, 0). samples.baseline Vector Sample IDs indexes corresponding baseline. samples.condition1 Vector Sample IDs indexes corresponding first condition. samples.condition2 Vector Sample IDs indexes corresponding second condition (optional). samples.condition3 Vector Sample IDs indexes corresponding third condition (optional).

title: Find detectable genes across comparisons. — detect_filter
text: named list. Always contains: $Comparison1: Data frame detectable genes df.BvsA. $DetectGenes: Character vector unique detectable gene IDs across comparisons. df.CvsA provided, also contains $Comparison2. df.DvsA provided, also contains $Comparison3.

what: Extract gene members from pathway analysis results — getgenesPA

text: gene set pathway analysis results table, retrieves leading edge genes, user-defined top fraction genes, genes gene set, combination. gene lists ordered rank provided ranked gene list.

title: Extract gene members from pathway analysis results — getgenesPA
code: getgenesPA(pa_data, geneset_list, ranked_genes, genes = c("all", "le"))

title: Extract gene members from pathway analysis results — getgenesPA
text: pa_data data frame pathway analysis results. Must always contain: NAME: gene set name. Additionally required depending genes: SIZE: number genes gene set. Required "le" "top". tags: numeric fraction (0-1) genes contributing enrichment score (GSEA leading edge). Produced automatically merge_PA(). Required genes = "le". top: numeric fraction (0-1) defining proportion top-ranked genes extract. Set manually user (e.g., pa_data$top <- 0.25 top 25%). Required genes = "top". Typically output merge_PA(). geneset_list named list gene sets, element character vector gene symbols. Typically output list_gmts(), use built-brca_geneset_list quick testing. ranked_genes character vector gene symbols ordered ranking metric (e.g., DESeq2 stat, log2FC, signal--noise ratio), positive negative. Non-significant genes fall middle list. Used order genes within extracted set. genes Character vector specifying extraction mode(s) use. combination "", "le", "top". Default: c("", "le").

title: Extract gene members from pathway analysis results — getgenesPA
text: Depends genes: Single mode (e.g., genes = "le"): named list element character vector gene symbols. list attribute genes_type used addgenesPA() name output column. Multiple modes (e.g., genes = c("", "le", "top")): named list one element per requested mode: $: named list gene set members. $le: named list leading edge genes (GSEA ). $top: named list top-ranked genes.

title: Extract gene members from pathway analysis results — getgenesPA
text: Three extraction modes: "le": GSEA output . Leading edge genes: subset genes drives enrichment signal. Size computed round(SIZE * tags), tags fraction gene hits (positive ES) (negative ES) peak running enrichment score. Definition GSEA User Guide: "percentage gene hits (positive ES) (negative ES) peak running enrichment score. gives indication percentage genes contributing enrichment score." (https://docs.gsea-msigdb.org/#GSEA/GSEA_User_Guide/). Requires columns SIZE tags pa_data, produced automatically merge_PA(). "top": enrichment result (GSEA, CAMERA, PADOG, etc.). user-defined top fraction genes ordered rank. Size computed round(SIZE * top), top numeric value 0 1 provided top column pa_data. represent true leading edge genes: flexible, rank-based selection suitable exploratory visualization pathway analysis method. Requires columns SIZE top pa_data. "": genes gene set, ordered rank.

title: Extract gene members from pathway analysis results — getgenesPA
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ data(gsea_results) data(brca_geneset_list) data(brca_rna_dea_tumor_vs_normal)  #or gsl <- list_gmts("path/to/gmt_folder/")  ranked    <- brca_rna_dea_tumor_vs_normal$gene_id[order(brca_rna_dea_tumor_vs_normal$stat,                                           decreasing = TRUE)] pa_single <- gsea_results[gsea_results$COMPARISON == "TumorVsNormal", ]  # ── GSEA results: all three modes available gene_lists <- getgenesPA(pa_single, brca_geneset_list, ranked,                          genes = c("all", "le", "top"))  # But first add the top column (e.g. top 30% of genes by rank) pa_single$top <- 0.30 gene_lists <- getgenesPA(pa_single, brca_geneset_list, ranked,                          genes = c("all", "le", "top"))  gene_lists$le[["KEGG_APOPTOSIS"]]    # leading edge genes gene_lists$top[["KEGG_APOPTOSIS"]]   # top 30% by rank gene_lists$all[["KEGG_APOPTOSIS"]]   # all genes  pa_annot <- addgenesPA(pa_single, gene_lists) head(pa_annot[, c("NAME", "all_genes", "le_genes", "top_genes")])  # ── CAMERA results: use "top" (no leading edge available) ─── data(brca_pa_results) camera_pa      <- brca_pa_results colnames(camera_pa)[colnames(camera_pa) == "GeneSet"] <- "NAME" camera_pa$SIZE <- sapply(camera_pa$NAME,                          function(x) length(brca_geneset_list[[x]])) camera_pa$top  <- 0.25   # top 25% by rank  gene_lists_cam <- getgenesPA(camera_pa, brca_geneset_list, ranked,                              genes = c("all", "top")) pa_annot_cam   <- addgenesPA(camera_pa, gene_lists_cam) head(pa_annot_cam[, c("NAME", "all_genes", "top_genes")]) } # }

title: Fit Cox Proportional Hazards Models and Return a Tidy Table — get_cox
text: Fits Cox proportional hazards models selected survival endpoint returns tidy table hazard ratios, confidence intervals, p-values, model metadata, labels ready plotted nice_forest().

title: Fit Cox Proportional Hazards Models and Return a Tidy Table — get_cox
code: get_cox(   data,   time_col = "PFI.time",   event_col = "PFI",   vars = NULL,   model = c("univariable", "multivariable", "adjusted"),   adjust_vars = NULL,   keep_adjust_terms = FALSE,   ref_levels = NULL,   min_n = 10,   min_n_per_level = 5,   min_events = 5,   min_events_per_level = 5,   exclude_survival_like = TRUE,   verbose = TRUE )

title: Fit Cox Proportional Hazards Models and Return a Tidy Table — get_cox
text: data data.frame containing survival columns (time_col, event_col) variables test. time_col Character. Name column follow-time. column numeric coercible numeric. Default: "PFI.time". event_col Character. Name event indicator column. coded 0 = censored 1 = event, coercible numeric 0/1. Default: "PFI". vars Character vector. Variables interest test. NULL, variables selected automatically excluding survival columns, ID-like columns, columns starting "_", optionally survival/outcome-like columns. model Character. Type Cox model fit. One "univariable", "multivariable", "adjusted". "univariable" fits one model per variable. "multivariable" fits one model containing variables vars. "adjusted" fits one model per variable interest, adjusted adjust_vars. adjust_vars Character vector. Covariates used model = "adjusted". Ignored "univariable" "multivariable" models. Default: NULL. keep_adjust_terms Logical. TRUE model = "adjusted", adjustment covariate terms kept returned table. FALSE, terms variable interest returned. Default: FALSE. ref_levels named list explicitly set reference levels categorical variables. Names must column names values must desired reference categories. Example: list(ER_Status_nature2012 = "Negative",            AJCC_Stage_nature2012 = "Stage "). min_n Integer. Minimum total number complete observations required Cox model. Default: 10. min_n_per_level Integer. categorical predictors, minimum number complete observations required category. Default: 5. Set 0 disable. min_events Integer. Minimum total number events required Cox model. Default: 5. Set 0 disable. min_events_per_level Integer. categorical predictors, minimum number events required category. main safeguard sparse categories infinite Cox coefficients. Default: 5. Set 0 disable. exclude_survival_like Logical. TRUE vars = NULL, automatic variable selection excludes columns whose names suggest survival endpoints outcome leakage, OS, DSS, DFI, PFI, days_to, death, vital_status, followup, survival. Default: TRUE. verbose Logical. TRUE, prints informative messages models variables skipped. Default: TRUE.

title: Fit Cox Proportional Hazards Models and Return a Tidy Table — get_cox
text: data.frame one row per model term columns including model, model_id, variable, term, term_clean, reference, HR, CI_low, CI_high, p.value, n_used, n_events, adjusted_for.

title: Fit Cox Proportional Hazards Models and Return a Tidy Table — get_cox
text: function performs several checks fitting model: Removes empty strings incomplete rows. Converts character logical predictors factors. Drops unused factor levels. Applies explicit reference levels via ref_levels. Skips sparse categorical variables using min_n_per_level min_events_per_level. Skips models possible perfect separation infinite coefficients. Returns exponentiated Cox coefficients hazard ratios. function, "multivariable" means Cox model multiple predictors one survival endpoint. different "multivariate", usually refers multiple outcomes.

title: Fit Cox Proportional Hazards Models and Return a Tidy Table — get_cox
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Univariable Cox models cox_uni <- get_cox(   data = df,   time_col = "PFI.time",   event_col = "PFI",   vars = c("ER_Status_nature2012", "PAM50Call_RNAseq"),   model = "univariable" )  # Multivariable Cox model cox_multi <- get_cox(   data = df,   time_col = "PFI.time",   event_col = "PFI",   vars = c("age_at_initial_pathologic_diagnosis",            "AJCC_Stage_nature2012",            "PAM50Call_RNAseq"),   model = "multivariable" )  # Adjusted Cox models cox_adj <- get_cox(   data = df,   time_col = "PFI.time",   event_col = "PFI",   vars = c("ER_Status_nature2012", "HER2_Final_Status_nature2012"),   adjust_vars = c("age_at_initial_pathologic_diagnosis",                   "AJCC_Stage_nature2012"),   model = "adjusted" )  nice_forest(cox_adj) } # }

what: Function to Fit a GLM and Return Tidy Results with Effect Sizes and FDR Correction — get_glm
title: Function to Fit a GLM and Return Tidy Results with Effect Sizes and FDR Correction — get_glm
text: Fits Generalized Linear Model (GLM) binary, continuous, count, proportion, rate, positive skewed outcomes, depending specified family. function returns tidy tibble coefficients, optional exponentiated effect sizes, 95% confidence intervals, Wald test statistics, raw p-values, multiple-testing-adjusted q-values. fitted glm object attached attribute can passed directly downstream functions nice_ROC without re-fitting.

title: Function to Fit a GLM and Return Tidy Results with Effect Sizes and FDR Correction — get_glm
code: get_glm(   data,   outcome,   predictors,   family = "binomial",   adjust_method = "BH",   conf_level = 0.95,   exponentiate = NULL,   remove_intercept = TRUE,   verbose = FALSE )

title: Function to Fit a GLM and Return Tidy Results with Effect Sizes and FDR Correction — get_glm
text: data data.frame tibble containing outcome predictor variables. outcome Character string length 1. Name outcome column. logistic regression typically coded 0/1, although binomial formats accepted glm can also used. predictors Character vector. Names predictor columns include. Categorical variables factor character; handled glm contrast coding automatically. family Character string, family function, family object passed glm. specifies assumed distribution outcome link function used GLM. Common options include: "binomial" binomial(link = "logit") binary, proportion, success/failure outcomes; corresponds logistic regression link "logit". "gaussian" gaussian(link = "identity") approximately normally distributed continuous outcomes. "poisson" poisson(link = "log") count rate outcomes. "quasibinomial" "quasipoisson" binomial Poisson-type outcomes overdispersion. Gamma(link = "log") positive, right-skewed continuous outcomes. inverse.gaussian() positive continuous outcomes variance increasing strongly mean. Custom family objects can also supplied. Default: "binomial". adjust_method Character string. Method p-value adjustment passed p.adjust. Options: "BH", "bonferroni", "holm", "", "fdr", "none". Default: "BH". conf_level Numeric value (0, 1). Confidence level interval. Default: 0.95. exponentiate Logical NULL. TRUE, coefficients confidence intervals exponentiated. NULL, exponentiation applied automatically model link "logit" "log". gives odds ratios logistic models logit link, rate ratios Poisson-type models log link, multiplicative effects log-link models. Default: NULL. remove_intercept Logical. Whether drop (Intercept) row returned table. Default: TRUE. verbose Logical. TRUE, prints model summary console. Default: FALSE.

title: Function to Fit a GLM and Return Tidy Results with Effect Sizes and FDR Correction — get_glm
text: tibble class c("get_glm_result", "tbl_df", "tbl", "data.frame") following columns: term Predictor name; factors, includes level according contrast coding used glm. estimate Exponentiated coefficient exponentiate = TRUE; otherwise raw coefficient model linear predictor scale. ci_lower Lower bound confidence interval scale estimate. ci_upper Upper bound confidence interval scale estimate. std_error Standard error coefficient linear predictor scale. statistic Wald test statistic. fixed-dispersion families binomial Poisson typically z-statistic; families estimated dispersion may t-statistic. p_value Two-sided p-value Wald test. q_value P-value adjusted multiple comparisons using method specified adjust_method. significance Star annotation based raw p-value: "***" p<0.001, "**" p<0.01, "*" p<0.05, "." p<0.10, " " otherwise. following attributes attached returned object: model fitted glm object. formula Character string model formula. family Family name used. link Link function used. n_obs Number observations used model fitting. AIC Akaike Information Criterion. May NA quasi-likelihood families. exponentiate Logical indicating whether coefficients exponentiated. adjust_method P-value adjustment method used.

title: Function to Fit a GLM and Return Tidy Results with Effect Sizes and FDR Correction — get_glm
text: Q-values computed across reported terms removing intercept remove_intercept = TRUE. Therefore, multiple-testing correction pool matches number hypotheses shown returned table. Automatic exponentiation based link function. Models logit link reported odds ratios; models log link reported multiplicative effects rate ratios mean ratios. Models identity, probit, cloglog, inverse, links exponentiated automatically.

title: Function to Fit a GLM and Return Tidy Results with Effect Sizes and FDR Correction — get_glm
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Binary outcome: logistic regression res_logit <- get_glm(   data       = train_data,   outcome    = "stage_advanced",   predictors = c("age", "ER", "PR", "HER2", "histology", "menopause"),   family     = "binomial" )  # Continuous outcome: linear model through glm res_gaussian <- get_glm(   data       = train_data,   outcome    = "tumor_size",   predictors = c("age", "ER", "PR", "HER2"),   family     = "gaussian" )  # Count outcome: Poisson regression res_pois <- get_glm(   data       = train_data,   outcome    = "n_mutations",   predictors = c("age", "stage", "histology"),   family     = "poisson" )  # Positive skewed continuous outcome res_gamma <- get_glm(   data       = train_data,   outcome    = "cost",   predictors = c("age", "stage", "treatment"),   family     = Gamma(link = "log") )  # Retrieve fitted model fit <- attr(res_logit, "model") } # }

title: Detect gene set communities and generate super-term labels — get_network_communities

title: Detect gene set communities and generate super-term labels — get_network_communities
text: x JaccardResult object (output geneset_similarity()). threshold Numeric 0 1. Gene set pairs Jaccard similarity value connected network. Default: 0.3. method Character. Community detection algorithm use. One : "louvain" — igraph::cluster_louvain(): fast, recommended use cases. Default. "fast_greedy" — igraph::cluster_fast_greedy(): optimizes modularity greedily, works well mid-size networks. "walktrap" — igraph::cluster_walktrap(): random-walk approach, tends find smaller, tighter communities. superterms Logical. TRUE, calls get_superterm() includes output $superterms. Default: TRUE. n_terms Integer. Number top TF-IDF terms per super-term label. Passed get_superterm(). Default: 3. remove_prefix Logical. Remove database prefix first underscore (e.g., "KEGG_"). Passed get_superterm(). Default: TRUE. seed Integer. Random seed reproducible community detection. Default: 174.

title: Detect gene set communities and generate super-term labels — get_network_communities
text: named list four elements: $communities: igraph communities object. $membership: Named integer vector community IDs, one per gene set. $adjacency_matrix: Binary matrix (1 Jaccard > threshold). $superterms: Output get_superterm() $mapping $summary. NULL superterms = FALSE.

title: Detect gene set communities and generate super-term labels — get_network_communities
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ gsl <- list_gmts("path/to/gmt_folder/") res <- read.csv("path/to/results.csv")  # Full workflow jac   <- geneset_similarity(gsl, res, fdr_th = 0.05) clust <- do_clust(jac) net   <- get_network_communities(jac, threshold = 0.3, method = "louvain")  net$membership            # community ID per gene set net$superterms$mapping    # gene set -> superterm net$superterms$summary    # community sizes and labels  # Pass results to network plots plots <- network_clust_gg(   jac,   clust_result   = clust,   superterms     = TRUE,   superterm_data = net$superterms ) plots$combined } # }

Typically output igraph::membership() applied community detection result (e.g., igraph::cluster_louvain()). Must length geneset_names. See get_network_communities() simpler workflow. n_terms Integer. Number top TF-IDF terms include label. Default: 3. remove_prefix Logical. TRUE, removes text first underscore gene set names (e.g., strips "KEGG_" prefix "KEGG_GLYCOLYSIS"). Default: TRUE.

title: Generate representative super-term labels for gene set communities — get_superterm
text: named list two elements: $mapping: tibble::tibble() columns geneset, community, superterm — one row per gene set, sorted community. $summary: tibble::tibble() columns community, superterm, n_genesets — one row per community, sorted decreasing size.

title: Generate representative super-term labels for gene set communities — get_superterm
text: TF-IDF works : gene set name treated document word term. TF-IDF upweights words frequent within community rare across communities, making resulting label specific cluster rather generic. frequency-based fallback used TF-IDF returns terms (e.g., small communities). Common pathway words ("pathway", "signaling", "regulation", etc.) standard English stopwords removed scoring. Note: function easily used get_network_communities(), handles community detection calls get_superterm() internally. prefer call directly, need community membership vector:
code: adj        <- (jac$jaccard_sim > 0.3) * 1 g          <- igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix(adj, mode = "undirected") comm       <- igraph::cluster_louvain(g) membership <- igraph::membership(comm)  st <- get_superterm(   geneset_names        = names(membership),   community_membership = membership )

code: merge_PA(input_directory, fdr_replace = 0.001)

title: Merge GSEA result files into a single data frame — merge_PA
text: input_directory Character. Path directory containing one GSEA collection result files .tsv format (e.g., output GSEA_merge.sh). file must end .tsv. fdr_replace Numeric. Value used replace FDR q-val = 0. occurs permutation produced NES extreme observed one, meaning true FDR 1 / n_permutations. standard 1,000 permutations, recommended value 0.001. Adjust 1 / n_permutations different number permutations used. Default: 0.001.

title: Merge GSEA result files into a single data frame — merge_PA
text: data frame (gsea_data) containing merged processed GSEA results standardized column names.

title: Merge GSEA result files into a single data frame — merge_PA
text:
Input file format: .tsv file corresponds one MSigDB collection (e.g., H.tsv, C2.tsv) must follow standard GSEA output format following columns: NAME: gene set name. SIZE: number genes gene set. ES: enrichment score. NES: normalized enrichment score. NOM p-val: nominal p-value. FDR q-val: false discovery rate. Values exactly 0 indicate permutation produced equally extreme NES (.e., true FDR permutation resolution 1 / n_permutations). replaced fdr_replace avoid -Inf log-transforms. FWER p-val: family-wise error rate. RANK MAX: gene rank maximum enrichment score. LEADING EDGE: string encoding leading edge statistics format "tags=XX%, list=XX%, signal=XX%". Parsed three numeric columns: tags (fraction gene set leading edge), list (fraction ranked list used), signal (enrichment signal strength). Comparison: name comparison (e.g., "TumorVsNormal"). Renamed COMPARISON output. Required visualization splot_PA() multiplot_PA() . GS
follow link MSigDB GS DETAILS: removed automatically. Output columns: input columns (minus two removed ) plus: COLLECTION: name MSigDB collection, derived file name removing .tsv suffix. tags, list, signal: numeric leading edge components (0-1 scale). Log10FDR: -log10(FDR) computed applying fdr_replace. FDR: renamed FDR q-val. COMPARISON: renamed Comparison.

title: Merge GSEA result files into a single data frame — merge_PA
text: input .tsv files must contain Comparison column identifying comparison (e.g., "TumorVsNormal"). column renamed COMPARISON output required splot_PA() multiplot_PA()  operate multi-comparison mode. files come single comparison column, add manually file merging: your_data$Comparison <- "YourComparisonName".

title: Pathway analysis visualization across multiple comparisons — multiplot_PA
text: data data frame pathway analysis results containing two comparisons. Typically output merge_PA(). comparison_col Name column identifying comparison. Appears x-axis facet. Default: "COMPARISON". facet_col Name column used define facets  one facet per unique value. Can original gene set name column (e.g., "NAME") manually curated column cleaner shorter labels (e.g., "clean_name"). Default: "NAME". axis_y Name column use y-axis. Default: "NES". fdr_col Name column containing FDR values. -log10(FDR) computed internally used fill color. Default: "FDR". comparison_order Character vector specifying left--right order comparisons x-axis facet. example, comparison_order = c("BvsA", "CvsA") places BvsA left CvsA right. NULL (default), order follows factor levels comparison_col appear data. custom_labels Named character vector x-axis tick labels. Useful shortening comparison names axis. example, custom_labels = c(TumorVsNormal = "Tumor", MetastasisVsNormal = "Mets"). Default: NULL. ncol_wrap Integer. Number columns facet_wrap. Default: 2. free_y Logical. TRUE, facet uses y-axis scale. Default: TRUE. fill_limits Numeric vector length 2 setting color scale range -log10(FDR). Values outside range clamped nearest limit. example, fill_limits = c(0, 5) maps gene sets -log10(FDR) >= 5 (FDR <= 0.00001) maximum red, value 0 white. Useful one gene set extreme significance makes rest appear uniform. Default: NULL (auto). fill_palette Character vector two colors fill gradient (low high -log10(FDR)). Default: c("white", "red"). theme_params Named list override default theme parameters. See Details.

Useful small samples; may hide real variability large samples. Default: FALSE. direction Character. Direction pROC::roc. Usually "auto" (default). Set "<" ">" need enforce direction. plot_title Character string. Main title figure. Default: "ROC Curve Comparison". plot_subtitle Character string NULL. Subtitle. Default: NULL. theme_fn ggplot2 theme function (without parentheses). Applied plot. Default: ggplot2::theme_classic. return_data Logical. TRUE, returns named list containing ggplot object underlying data/statistics. FALSE (default), ggplot object returned.

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # split_cases requires three DESeq2 comparisons. # Simulate a 3-phenotype study: Normal (A), Primary (B), Metastasis (C) set.seed(174) n_genes <- 500  make_res <- function(seed) {   set.seed(seed)   data.frame(     ensembl        = paste0("ENSG", sprintf("%011d", seq_len(n_genes))),     log2FoldChange = rnorm(n_genes, 0, 1.5),     padj           = runif(n_genes, 0, 0.5),     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   ) }  df_BvsA <- make_res(1) df_CvsA <- make_res(2) df_BvsC <- make_res(3)  cases <- split_cases(   df.BvsA              = df_BvsA,   df.CvsA              = df_CvsA,   df.BvsC              = df_BvsC,   unique_id            = "ensembl",   significance_var     = "padj",   significance_cutoff  = 0.25,   change_var           = "log2FoldChange",   change_cutoff        = 0 )  # Number of genes per case sapply(cases, nrow)  # Inspect Case 1 (ladder genes: significant in all 3 comparisons) head(cases$Case1) } # }

title: Pathway analysis visualization for a single comparison — splot_PA
text: data data frame pathway analysis results single comparison. Typically output merge_PA() filtered one value COMPARISON column, results single CAMERA/GSEA run. Must contain columns specified geneset_col, collection_col, nes_col, fdr_col. geneset_col Name column containing gene set labels shown y-axis. Default: "NAME". collection_col Name column containing MSigDB collection labels used group gene sets (e.g., "KEGG", "HALLMARK", "GO"). Default: "COLLECTION". nes_col Name column containing NES values (x-axis). Default: "NES". fdr_col Name column containing FDR values. -log10(FDR) computed internally used fill color. Default: "FDR". order One "desc" "asc". Sort order NES values y-axis. Default: "desc". fill_limits Numeric vector length 2 setting color scale range -log10(FDR). Values outside range clamped nearest limit. example, fill_limits = c(0, 5) maps gene sets -log10(FDR) >= 5 (.e., FDR <= 0.00001) maximum color (red), value 0 minimum color (white). Useful gene sets extreme significance washes color variation rest. Default: NULL (auto  uses actual data range). fill_palette Character vector two colors fill gradient (low high -log10(FDR)). Default: c("white", "red"). top_n Integer. set, keep top top_n gene sets ranked abs(nes_col). Ignored top_n_per_direction set. Default: NULL (keep ). top_n_per_direction Integer. set, keep top N gene sets highest positive NES top N lowest (negative) NES separately, directions remain represented. Takes precedence top_n. Default: NULL (keep ). clean_labels Logical. TRUE, strip common MSigDB collection prefixes ("HALLMARK_", "KEGG_", "REACTOME_", "GOBP_", "GOCC_", "GOMF_") gene set names, replace underscores spaces, convert title case. Default: TRUE. label_wrap Integer. Character width gene set labels wrapped onto multiple lines. Default: 35. symmetric_x Logical. TRUE, x-axis (NES) range made symmetric around zero using largest absolute NES value data. Default: TRUE. theme_params Named list override default theme parameters. See Details.

code: data(vst_counts) data(sampledata)  # Dimensions dim(vst_counts) #> [1] 21330    32  # Value range (log2-like scale) range(vst_counts) #> [1]  1.784263 20.849634  # PCA plot colored by sample type colnames(sampledata)[colnames(sampledata) == "patient_id"] <- "id" nice_PCA(   object      = vst_counts,   annotations = sampledata,   variables   = c(fill = "sample_type"),   legend_names = c(fill = "Sample Type"),   colors      = c("steelblue", "firebrick"),   shapes      = c(21, 21),   title       = "TCGA-LUAD PCA" )   if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # UMAP plot colnames(sampledata)[colnames(sampledata) == "patient_id"] <- "id"  nice_UMAP(   object      = vst_counts,   annotations = sampledata,   variables   = c(fill = "sample_type"),   legend_names = c(fill = "Sample Type"),   colors      = c("steelblue", "firebrick"),   shapes      = c(21, 21),   title       = "TCGA-LUAD UMAP" )  # tSNE plot # perplexity must be lower than the number of samples divided by 3  colnames(sampledata)[colnames(sampledata) == "patient_id"] <- "id" nice_tSNE(   object       = vst_counts,   annotations  = sampledata,   perplexity   = 5,   variables    = c(fill = "sample_type"),   legend_names = c(fill = "Sample Type"),   colors       = c("steelblue", "firebrick"),   shapes       = c(21, 21),   title        = "TCGA-LUAD tSNE" ) } # }
